modelAnswers.answer: Down group 2 each atom has more electron shells, so the atomic radius grows and the outer electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded. The attraction on the outer electrons weakens, so they are lost more easily to form M2+ ions, and reactivity rises down the group.
modelAnswers.question: Magnesium reacts very slowly with cold water, but barium reacts vigorously. Explain this trend down group 2 in terms of atomic structure.

modelAnswers.answer: The ammonia molecules act as ligands: each donates a lone pair to the Cu2+ ion, forming coordinate bonds and replacing the water ligands in a ligand-exchange reaction, giving the deep blue [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ complex.
modelAnswers.question: Excess ammonia is added to aqueous copper(II) sulfate and the pale blue solution turns deep blue. Explain what the ammonia molecules do.

nextSteps: Reteach the zinc trap from the paired notes trap before any further transition-metal work: a transition metal forms a stable ion with a partially filled d subshell, and Zn2+ is 3d10, so zinc is excluded.
Practise explaining group trends with charge, radius and shielding, and check each claim against the period 3 trends in the notes.
strengths: Most of the class can explain reactivity down group 2, such as the group 2 answer on the worksheet: bigger atoms, more shielding, weaker nuclear attraction, outer electrons lost more easily.
The class can explain ligand exchange on the exit ticket: ammonia donates a lone pair to Cu2+, forming coordinate bonds and the deep blue complex.
